ranked_evidence.title: Sonia : Meaning and Origin of First Name
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Meaning of the first name  Sonia. The name Sonia has its origins in multiple cultures and languages, with its most notable roots traced back to the Greek name Sophia, which means "wisdom." The name Sonia is often considered a diminutive or variation of Sophia, particularly in Slavic languages, where it is prevalent. In various cultures, Sonia has been adopted as a standalone name, gaining popularity in different regions over the centuries. In addition to its Greek roots, the name has been associated with Latin influences, where it was adopted and adapted in several Western European languages. The name is often associated with cultural movements and the emergence of strong female characters in literature and media, which further enhanced its appeal. In terms of cultural significance, Sonia has been used in various artistic and literary contexts. In 1993, Sonia represented Britain in the Eurovision Song Contest, with ‘Better The Devil You Know’, but was beaten to the number one position by the Irish entry. Another Stock, Aitken And Waterman (SAW) pop protégée, Sonia had been singing around Liverpool clubs since leaving school and was a well known starlet in Merseyside having appeared as Adrian Boswell’s girlfriend in the hit UK television situation comedy Bread. He was impressed enough to get her on his television show The Hitman And Her and shortly afterwards she recorded her debut single, ‘You’ll Never Stop Me Loving You’.

In 1993, Sonia represented the United Kingdom in the Eurovision Song Contest 1993, singing the Dean Collinson and Brian Teasdale composition "Better the Devil You Know "Better the Devil You Know (Sonia song)")". Her third album, also titled *Better the Devil You Know "Better the Devil You Know (album)")* was released that year and reached number 32 in the UK.
